title: Tenant export sharding + differential delivery for very large CSV bundles
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Large enterprise tenants (500M+ tokens/day) produce gigantic daily usage files that exceed memory and upload time windows. Current exporter creates one monolithic CSV per tenant which causes long GC pauses, S3 multipart churn, and frequent failed uploads. We need a new delivery pattern that reduces tail latency, allows parallel consumers, and enables incremental (differential) exports to cut repeat data transfer for customers who only need deltas.

Proposal summary: Build a tenant-aware export sharder that slices a tenant's export window into multiple independently-writable shards (time-window + object key prefix). Each shard produces compressed CSV parts (gz) with stable schema. A manifest file lists shards and delta base references; customers can download full bundle or subscribe to differential deltas. We will also add a graceful webhook fallback for near-real-time customers and continue producing a legacy single-file bundle for compatibility for one major release.

Goals:
- Avoid single-process memory pressure for very large tenants
- Reduce S3 multipart upload failures by smaller parallel uploads
- Allow customers to fetch only changed rows using differential manifests
- Keep pricing/quotas transparent: same billable units but more manageable delivery units

Out of scope: complete UI in Console for showing shard indexes (separate follow-up ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Exporter can split a tenant daily export into N shards based on configurable shard-size target (e.g., ~1GB compressed)
Each shard is individually uploaded to S3 with idempotency tokens so repeated retries do not produce duplicates
A manifest JSON (s3://.../tenant/YYYY-MM-DD/manifest.json) lists shards with byte ranges, gz checksums, and optional parent snapshot id for diffs
Differential export API returns a list of changed shard ids since a checkpoint token; full bundle download still available
End-to-end test proves that a 20GB daily export can be delivered as 25 shards in <30 minutes total wall time using existing export fleet
Fallback webhook is created for customers who requested streaming delivery; webhook includes shard URLs and manifest link
Backwards compatibility: a compatibility-layer job generates legacy single CSV for customers marked legacy for 2 weeks post-rollout
technical_notes: Sharding key: primary by hour-window + deterministic hash(tenant_id) to distribute across workers; allow override for tenant-defined sharding policy
Write path: workers write CSV rows into local rotating buffers (streaming csv writer) that flush to temporary gz parts when buffer >= 64MB or after 90s
Upload: use S3 multipart with part size 32MB for parts >100MB; include x-amz-server-side-encryption header where tenant requires KMS
Idempotency: attach export_run_id + shard_id + part_index in S3 metadata and maintain idempotent part-completion markers in export metadata db

Differential algorithm: maintain per-tenant last-export-checkpoint (export_run_id). During run, compute row fingerprints (sha1 of stable key columns) and persist in small bloom filter + per-shard diff manifest; customers can request changed fingerprints via compact delta manifest
Cost: additional metadata storage estimated +2% across global exports; compute increase for fingerprinting ~10% CPU for large tenants

Observability: emit metrics: export.shards.started, export.shards.completed, export.shard.size_bytes, export.shard.upload_time_seconds, export.shard.retry_count; create dashboard and an alert on shard_upload_95p > 120s
Concurrency: bounded worker pool per-tenant adjustable by tenant SLA to avoid noisy neighbor effects
Retention: shard-level retention follows tenant retention policy; manifest points to s3 keys and may include presigned-url TTLs for one-off downloads
rollout_plan: Feature flag gated by tenant (console UI toggle) + default opt-out
Phase 1 (canary): enable for internal test accounts and 3 pilot customers with estimated >100GB/day usage
Phase 2: enable on signup for new large-tenant signups and gradually flip pilot customers after feedback
Phase 3: default for all tenants above threshold after 2 weeks of stable telemetry; run legacy single-file generator for 14 days for compatibility
Rollback: shorten retention of partial shards and mark export_run as failed if >50% shard failures; revert to legacy single-file generation path
backward_compatibility: Provide a compatibility daemon that consumes shard manifests and concatenates shards into the legacy single CSV for customers who still depend on that shape
Keep export API endpoints unchanged: export_id semantics preserved; customers receive a bundle URL that may point to the manifest (new) or legacy CSV (old)
Document new manifest schema in Confluence with examples and client-side sample code to reassemble CSVs
testing_notes: Unit: streaming csv writer edge cases (line breaks in fields, quotes) and gz checksum validation
Integration: simulate a 20GB export with ephemeral workers using test harness (localstack S3) and assert time-to-complete and shard counts
Chaos: force S3 part failures and verify idempotent retries and eventual consistency of manifest
Load: run 10 parallel large-tenant exports to ensure global fleet autoscaling settings handle peak
E2E: pilot customer acceptance test where they consume differential manifests and verify delta size <= 20% of full bundle for typical churn rates
comments: 2026-02-25 Miguel Torres: Initial spike completed. Verified streaming writer can keep memory <200MB while writing 10GB of rows. Next: wire up multi-part upload and idempotency metadata.
2026-03-02 Aisha Patel: Design review notes from PM - ensure delta manifest supports row-level tombstones for deletes. Also request for audit-log entry per manifest publish.
2026-03-04 Reviewer (Infra): Use 32MB multipart part size rather than 16MB to reduce API calls. Also prefer TransferAcceleration off unless region-limited customers request it.
2026-03-08 QA (Samir Gupta): Found race where worker could double-flush a buffer during graceful shutdown - fixed by using flush-in-progress mutex. Added regression test.

2026-03-11 Miguel Torres: Canary run with internal pilot (tenant-qa-3) showed 18 shards (approx 700MB each compressed), total wall time 21m, 0 failed parts. Preparing to enable pilot customers next week.
2026-03-12 PM (Evelyn Cho): Approved pilot customer list; asked to include one customer behind strict VPC egress rules to validate private deployment path
